title: The Knee That Clicks
subject: a wife who says she can find her husband in a dark house by the click of his left knee on every step, and he takes her out dancing on their anniversary so she can hear it keep time
caption: Big band swing, 1950s Sinatra-era style. Muted trumpet section stabs, warm saxophone section pads and unison lines, walking upright bass, swung brushed drums with ride cymbal, stride piano fills. Lush live big band recording with natural room reverb. Male baritone, clearly sung melody, full open tone, relaxed swing phrasing. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 132 BPM, B-flat major. Warm, affectionate, smiling. No synths, no electric guitar, no autotune, no hip-hop beats, no modern pop drums.
lyrics:
[Intro - sax section, walking bass]

[Verse 1]
My left knee clicks on every stair
It's done it since I was forty
The doctor says it's only air
And tells me not to worry

[Pre-Chorus]
But you say in the dark you know it's me
Before I reach the landing

[Chorus]
Click, click, there goes my knee
You say it's how you find me
You don't need the hallway light
You just listen for the clicking

[Verse 2]
So Saturday I booked a band
And a table by the floor
I took you gently by the hand
Like thirty years before

[Pre-Chorus]
And over all the trumpets playing
You heard my knee keep time

[Chorus]
Click, click, there goes my knee
And you're laughing on my shoulder
Every step is one more year
And it clicks a little louder

[Outro - brass swell, brushed drums]
Click, click, darling, dance with me
